comments.author: @OscarTheStrategist
comments.text:
To effectively understand (and sometimes even, join) this conversation, we first need to let go of our very engrained social biases. Nerds aren't inherently good guys, or even relatively harmless. Regulation isn't inherently bad, nor does it have to be absolute. Things are so much into the grey area, that we're struggling to have effective conversations about these things because of our need to "pick a side" - and the people currently in power know this. They have known it for a very long time, and the way they continue to stay in power is by benefiting from either side of the coin flip.

You may think I just said a bunch of nothing, so I'll leave you with this:

The biggest question is not alignment... but Open Sourcing powerful technology like AGI (ASI for some).

Open source means a single entity (person or company or country or group) POTENTIALLY CANNOT exert their own will with the (potentially limitless) power of a true AGI (or ASI).

Open source means also that random bad actors can easily wield said power and use it for destructive purposes inevitably.

That is the crux of the issue.

That issue is what raises all of these other (mostly valid) questions about absolute power, or near-absolute power.

Here's the thing: I'm of the opinion that we're too late, and that a large portion of these public virtual signaling is just for show. 

Remember that the original jailbreak due to context window was done to us humans with the advent of mass media. IFKYK

In the end, I don't have the answers. I just wish that there was a better way to have important conversations about AI safety and regulation without having to "pick a side" - not even a made-up side like "we're on the side of humanity" - that's BS. Technology that assures dominance will continue to be created by the powers that be, FOR the powers that be.

Do we have the power to decide who or what those ruling the world will be? - Yes, theoretically. 

In practice, though, we depend so much on technology (not just computers, but communication, transportation, energy, etc.) that we have effectively given up control in the name of convenience, and THAT is what scares me. No, I'm not a doomer, or a tech evangelist or apologist. Neither am I saying we should go back to the days of hunter/gatherers.

I'm just a father who wishes for a future where an intelligent life like my children and your children can exist without so much oppression from THE POWERS THAT BE.

comments.author: @EarlWagner
comments.text:
@WesRoth Hey Wes! I've been a big fan of your channel for a while and regularly watch videos. I wanted to provide some feedback on this video regarding EA. I hope it could be pinned to help provide an alternative perspective against some of the unintentional misinformation posted and help people be less likely to draw incorrect conclusions. I doubt that taking down this video or re-wording parts will be within your scope of consideration but hopefully pinning this will be because I don't believe that you intentionally wanted to pass on bad information or help people draw bad conclusions about EA.

I have considered myself and EA for a long time even before the term EA was registered in my mind. The idea of using Evidence and Reason to try to figure out the most good you can do as opposed to simply just selecting some sort of good (an intervention within a problem area) based on how it makes you feel or from simply following someone else's request (like the spam emails in an example you used) is what I believe everyone should strive to do. It's not enough to simply believe that what you believe or support does good, but to actually try to verify that it does good and see how much good it does compared to other solutions. 

1. EA is not a unified system. After attending EA Global conferences, local EA meetups, running my own EA meetups (in person and irl), and consuming a variety of EA related content, I can thoroughly attest that there is not one specific thing all EA's focus on and not just one solution that is promoted. Within EA people have different cause areas they care about more than others and often promote different solutions for different reasons. This is the same even within AI related concerns within EA. EA is not a single org. It is an idea about trying to use evidence and reason to do the most good. There are many orgs within EA that focus on many causes areas and/or across cause areas. 

2. Correlation and Causation. Just because someone performs/promotes a "bad" activity and they happen to be associated with some other belief/activity does not mean that what they are associated with was the cause. SBF doing something bad or another person/org that might do/promote something bad, and they happen to both support EA, doesn't mean EA is the cause. Unfortunately it can become easy to associate things like this often leading to the "Guilty by Association" fallacy. Once a negative association has been formed it can easily lead to the "Genetic" fallacy where people then outright dismiss anything associated with EA. Then there are those who will build on top of this existing negative association and/or provide only additional negative information to try to implement "Poisoning the Well" arguments to discredit EA. 

The way the information was provided, especially when it is impacting something they deeply care about, can easily lead people to adopt negative beliefs against EA. I don't believe that was your intention though.

I personally know a lot of EA's and EA Orgs that do not promote slowing down or banning/stopping outright all AI Research and actively invest in AI Research in order to help achieve the most good. Yes a major focus of nearly all EA's is to try to reduce Existential Risk. AI can be used to help do that but it can also be used to actively work against that. The ideas are to try to openly identify, research, discuss, and evaluate solutions to the positive and negative risk that AI may contain. Not everyone in EA therefore supports these different ideas being discussed. 

To find evidence of the diversified opinions within EA you can view the EA Forums, Less Wrong Forums, the AI Alignment Forums, etc. There are a lot cross posts between an abundance of AI Researchers, Software Developers, general Science Researchers, social impact orgs, etc between those forums and other places.

Oh an there are also various definitions of what an "Existential Risk" is that many groups within and outside of EA try to work with and improve over time.

comments.text:
AGI is an existential risk because it is completely outside the realm of anything we as a species have ever dealt with, or, I would say, are even capable of dealing with considering the current maturity we have as a species.

Imagine how long it takes a human to become a productive, economically useful worker.  The answer is roughly 20 - 25 years.  Now, consider how long it takes an AGI to become productive and economically useful.  The answer is about a minute (however long it takes to copy a model to a new gpu).  This is already a scale of 10 million to 1 in the favor of AI.  Now, consider how AI learns vs how a human learns.  A human has a subjective, first-person experience where we absorb knowledge slowly.  And, more importantly, we absorb knowledge individually.  That is, if I suddenly know a fact, it does not at all imply that anyone else knows the fact.  I can teach someone else, of course, but that takes time for both of us.  At the limit, humans learning something is O(n), where n is the number of humans.  

Now, compare that to AI.  A hivemind of agents can result in each individual agent gaining new experiences, which can then be propagated to all other agents via a single model update.  The time to learn a new fact is no longer O(n), it becomes O(1) -- all it would take is a single model to learn something, at which point said knowledge can be propagated to every other instance.

And, this is not even addressing the true existential risks.  An AI that is as capable as a large collection of humans can somewhat trivially modify its own source code -- even today LLMs today are capable of programming, this isn't science fiction.  If you see a human, you can at least infer some things about them.  How they think, what their lives might be like, the fact that they breathe, eat, etc.  If you see a self-modifying AI, you literally can't infer anything about it at all.  Its objective function could be changed to something completely different and completely inscrutable to us.  Maybe its benign, maybe its useful, maybe its absolutely horrendous.  We literally have no clue what it will do.

And that's my point.  AGI is an existential risk because its power is so far above what a human, or even all of humankind, is capable of that it is literally gambling with our future and just sort of hoping things turn out okay.
